exercise.name: Kettlebell Double Push Press

reference.title: Kettlebell Double Push Press
reference.listing: Video (movement reference; the page could not be read at authoring time because the proxy blocked it, so the movement was taken from the exercise name and standard coaching)

exercise.mechanics: Compound (leg drive, then shoulder and elbow press)

breathing.pattern: Breathe in and brace in the rack, keep the brace through the dip and drive, breathe out at the lockout, breathe in as the bells come down.
breathing.cadence: About 0.4 s dip, 0.55 s drive and press, 1.25 s back to the rack

prescription.tempo: Quick dip, explosive drive, controlled lowering
prescription.load: User-chosen pair of kettlebells; heavier than you can strict press, light enough that the dip stays short and upright
prescription.progression: Add reps, then heavier bells; then double jerk

cues.text: Feet about hip width, both kettlebells racked: fists in front of the shoulders, elbows down against the ribs, wrists straight.
Brace and dip quickly a few centimetres by bending the knees; trunk stays upright, heels down.
Drive hard through the legs and let the bells pop off the shoulders; finish the press with the arms.
Lock out overhead, biceps by the ears, ribs down, glutes tight.
Bring the bells back to the rack under control, absorbing them with soft knees.
Re-brace in the rack and repeat.

mistakes.mistake: Dipping too deep or leaning forward in the dip
mistakes.fix: Short, quick knee bend with the trunk vertical; the bells stay on the shoulders.
Let the leg drive launch the bells, then press.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back at the lockout
mistakes.fix: Squeeze the glutes and keep the ribs down.
Keep the elbows tucked against the ribs so the forearms are vertical.

kinematics.norm: A short, quick knee bend with an upright trunk; the push press dip is far shallower than a squat (clinical opinion)
Kettlebells resting on the forearms in front of the shoulders, elbows down (clinical opinion)
Arms fully extended overhead, the load stacked over the hips and ankles (CrossFit 2019, thruster lockout)
Fast dip and drive, controlled lowering (clinical opinion); standing presses gave higher deltoid activity than seated ones (Saeterbakken 2013)

sources.title: GymVisual 13775, Kettlebell Double Push Press, video (movement reference)
CrossFit 2019, The Thruster (CrossFit Essentials, coaching article, 12 April 2019)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The kettlebell load is user-chosen: pick bells you can lock out with control.
Fast lift: clear the space around you; if a bell gets away, step away from it.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
modify: Shoulder discomfort overhead: press only to the top of the head and keep the palms facing in.
Low-back discomfort: lighter bells and a firmer glute squeeze at the lockout.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover of the press; standing presses gave higher deltoid activity than seated presses (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover of the press; standing presses gave higher deltoid activity than seated presses (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Raises the upper arms as the elbows move out past the face (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Raises the upper arms as the elbows move out past the face (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_r: Drive the bells off the shoulders from the dip (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.quads_l: Drive the bells off the shoulders from the dip (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Hip extension in the drive and a tight lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_l: Hip extension in the drive and a tight lockout (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blades overhead (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_r: Finish the leg drive onto the balls of the feet briefly (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.calves_l: Finish the leg drive onto the balls of the feet briefly (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Keeps the trunk rigid in the dip and stops the low back arching overhead (clinical opinion).
